description: Stack-agnostic clustering & seeding rules consumed by the sf-srs drafting flow (`srs-cli.sh draft --from codebase`). The finding `kind`s below are CONCEPTS, not frameworks: `endpoint` = any invocable operation boundary (HTTP route, RPC/Tauri command, CLI command, gRPC method, queue/event handler, serverless function); `entity` = any persistent record type (SQL DDL/migrations, any ORM model, a struct backing a store, a protobuf message); `ui-flow` = any user-facing view (web/native/TUI/CLI). The deterministic CLI scanner recognises a SUBSET of stacks today (NestJS controllers, React pages, Prisma models, Jest/Vitest tests) and returns sparse findings on others — when that happens the AGENT supplements by reading the project's own operation/model registry directly (e.g. a Tauri `generate_handler!` list, a Go router, a FastAPI app, SQL migrations). SKILL.md points to this file; edit here, not in prose.

finding_kinds.source: An externally-invocable operation / command boundary. The scanner detects NestJS @Controller methods today; the same concept covers HTTP routes (Express/Fastify/Flask/Gin/Rails), RPC & Tauri commands, CLI subcommands, gRPC methods, message/queue handlers, and serverless functions. When the scanner is blind to the stack, enumerate these from the project's own registry (route table, command-handler list, etc.).
finding_kinds.area_heuristic: The nearest structural unit that groups the operation in THIS project: module / package / crate / feature folder (e.g. src/modules/<area>/, src-tauri/src/<area>/, internal/<area>/, app/<area>/, cmd/<area>/). Use the repo's own convention, not a fixed path.

finding_kinds.source: A user-facing view, screen, or flow. The scanner detects routed React pages today; the same concept covers Vue/Svelte/Angular routes, native screens (SwiftUI/Jetpack Compose), desktop windows, TUI views, and CLI subcommands with real UX.
finding_kinds.area_heuristic: The view's feature folder or route group (e.g. src/pages/<area>/, screens/<area>/, the route segment). Use the repo's own convention.

finding_kinds.source: A persistent data model / record type. The scanner detects Prisma `model` blocks today; the same concept covers SQL DDL & migrations, TypeORM/Sequelize/Drizzle/SQLAlchemy/Ecto/Diesel/ActiveRecord models, structs backing a store, and protobuf/IDL messages.
finding_kinds.area_heuristic: Map the model name to the domain it serves (e.g. User→accounts, Session→auth, Recording→capture). Use the project's own naming.

finding_kinds.source: An automated test case. The scanner detects Jest/Vitest `describe` / `it` / `test` today; the same concept covers Rust `#[test]` & integration tests, Go `testing`, pytest, JUnit, RSpec, and Playwright/Cypress e2e.
finding_kinds.area_heuristic: src/modules/<area>/, the tested unit's folder, or the filename stem. Use the repo's own layout.

finding_kinds.source: Project documentation: README, CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md, docs/**/*.md, architecture decision records, design docs, BACKLOG / roadmap files.
finding_kinds.area_heuristic: folder or document name (docs, modules, the feature it describes).

reading_findings: Every shape has `kind` + `title` — use them for first-pass clustering.
`area` is the glue: findings that share an `area` usually belong to the same Epic / FR cluster.
`file` is the authoritative path — quote it back to the user when proposing a cluster.
`endpoint.hasTests` flags `true` when the same `area` has at least one test finding — use it to prime the TC section.
`ui-flow.linkedEndpointGuess` is a soft hint (filename / route substring match) — verify before trusting.
`doc-context.excerpt` is capped at 280 chars — treat it as a summary seed, not the full text.

Scanner coverage is stack-specific and best-effort: if `draft --from codebase` returns few or no `endpoint` / `entity` findings for a stack it doesn't parse (Rust/Tauri, Go, Python, mobile, raw SQL…), DO NOT conclude the surface is empty — read the project's own operation/model registry directly and synthesise the findings yourself before clustering.

steps.name: Group by area
steps.action: Collect every finding whose `area` matches — `area` is whatever structural unit the project uses (module, package, crate, feature folder), not a fixed `src/modules/` path. Add `doc-context` findings that share the area name or a parent folder. If scanner findings are sparse for this stack, first enumerate the area's operations / models from the source tree yourself.

steps.name: Pick the Epic level
steps.action: One Epic per coherent area / domain (e.g. `auth`, `storage`, `capture`, `billing`). Title + narrative come from the richest `doc-context` in the group (README / CLAUDE.md / ADR), or from the user's wording.

steps.name: Propose the FRs
rules: One FR per `endpoint` / operation (or per tight cluster — CRUD or a command family on the same resource collapses into one FR).
Reuse `ui-flow` views / routes as acceptance criteria on the user-facing FR.
Populate `dsRefs` / `tcRefs` from the items seeded in step 4 so the FR surfaces traceability links.

steps.name: Seed the Epic-level DS / TC / NFR sections
steps.action: Every Epic carries the SRS five-category shape (UR + FR + DS + TC + NFR). See `templates/examples/example-epic.md` (rendered) and `templates/examples/example-epic.spec.json` (machine-readable) for the exact layout — the example uses a NestJS/Prisma/React auth module to stay concrete, but the spec format is stack-neutral. Apply the `seeding` rules below.

steps.name: Flag gaps
steps.action: Any operation with no matching test (`endpoint.hasTests=false`, or no `test` finding in the area) is a test-coverage gap — surface it as a **TODO** TC item (title `"<operation> — happy path"`, `expectedResult: "to write"`), not silently.

seeding.philosophy: Scanners surface raw material (and only for the stacks they parse); the agent synthesises items and fills the gaps for unparsed stacks. Reuse the L1+L2+L3 pattern from the eval: deterministic findings feed AI prompts, the agent always runs, the user always validates before write.

ds_items.description: One `DsItem` per material design decision visible in code — a data model, an operation's input/output contract, or a UI form — whatever the stack.

mappings.finding: entity — a persistent record type (Prisma/ORM model, SQL DDL, a struct backing a store, a protobuf message)
mappings.title: Data model — <EntityName>
mappings.description_source: fields + keys / uniqueness / relations (@id/@unique/@relation, PRIMARY KEY / FOREIGN KEY, struct tags) + soft-delete / deletedAt flag if present

mappings.finding: operation with a non-trivial input contract (HTTP body, RPC / command arguments, CLI flags) — ≥ 2 fields
mappings.title: API contract — <METHOD> <path>
mappings.description_source: input field list + validation rules surfaced by the stack's validators (class-validator, zod, serde, pydantic, struct tags)

mappings.finding: ui-flow with a form / input surface (≥ 2 fields)
mappings.title: UI form — <PageName>
mappings.description_source: form field list + the operation it submits to, if known

grouping_rules: Set `frRefs` to every FR in the group whose operation / entity / UI flow matches.
Deduplicate by title prefix — if two entities share the same core name (e.g. `User` + `UserProfile`), collapse into a single DS item with both sub-models listed in the description.

mappings.rule: parse Given/When/Then from the title if phrased that way, else bullet the `describe` chain

mappings.source: assertion in the test body (if readable)

todo_for_untested_endpoints.when: an operation (`endpoint`) with `hasTests=false`, or any operation in the area with no matching `test` finding
todo_for_untested_endpoints.emit_as: TODO TC item (the drift is auditable, not invisible)
reviewer_options: accept the TODO (making the gap part of the public contract)

nfr_items.description: NFRs are **proposed, not derived** — every seeded item must be marked for explicit human validation. Always emit with `priority: 'P3'` and `target: '<proposed — needs human validation>'`. The reviewer lifts priority / refines target before accepting. The signals below are stack-neutral: match the capability, not the framework.

layer1_stack_signals.signal: Authentication / session handling present — login, tokens, sessions, or credentials anywhere in the code (any stack: an /auth/* surface, a Session / RefreshToken record, an OAuth/JWT library, a stored password hash)
seeded_nfrs: Security — JWT access token expiry ≤ 15 min
Security — refresh token rotation on every use
Security — login rate limit ≤ 5 attempts / minute / IP

layer1_stack_signals.signal: Internationalisation present — locale files or an i18n library (i18next, gettext / .po, ICU, Fluent, a `locales/` folder), any stack
seeded_nfrs: i18n — all user-facing strings translated in FR + EN
a11y — locale switchable without restart / reload

layer1_stack_signals.signal: Persistent datastore present — SQL or NoSQL, via an ORM or raw migrations (Prisma, Drizzle, SQLAlchemy, Ecto, Diesel, SQLite, Postgres, Mongo…)
seeded_nfrs: Data — soft delete via deletedAt (or an equivalent retention policy) on user-owned entities
Data — schema migrations are reversible, or forward-only by explicit policy

layer1_stack_signals.signal: Hosted / always-on component — a container or orchestration manifest (Docker / Compose / k8s) or a health / readiness endpoint
seeded_nfrs: Ops — graceful shutdown drains in-flight work

layer1_stack_signals.signal: Automated end-to-end / integration suite present (Playwright, Cypress, Rust integration tests, pytest e2e, Detox…)
seeded_nfrs: Quality — e2e coverage on the critical user flows of the app

layer1_stack_signals.signal: Public API contract or schema artefact present (OpenAPI / Swagger, GraphQL schema, protobuf / IDL, a generated typed client)
seeded_nfrs: Docs — the API contract is regenerated on every change (CI guard)

layer1_stack_signals.signal: Local-first / on-device processing of user data — an offline app, or a core flow that runs without a server round-trip (desktop / mobile app, local model, local DB)
seeded_nfrs: Privacy — user data never leaves the device except on explicit, consented actions
Security — API keys & secrets stored in the OS keychain / secret manager, never in plaintext or VCS

layer1_stack_signals.signal: Native app requesting OS permissions — microphone, camera, screen capture, files, location, notifications
seeded_nfrs: Reliability — graceful degradation when a permission is denied (the feature stays usable in a reduced mode)
Security — request the least privilege needed and surface why each permission is asked

layer2_standard_saas_catalogue.nfr: Performance — define a responsiveness budget appropriate to the app (API p95 latency for services, interaction latency for UIs, throughput for batch / CLI) and hold it under expected load
Reliability — every failure path handled gracefully and actionably (no silent failures, no raw stack traces shown to users)
Security — secrets & credentials live in a secret manager / OS keychain, never plaintext or in version control

layer2_standard_saas_catalogue.condition: only for hosted or always-on components

layer2_standard_saas_catalogue.nfr: Privacy — sensitive / personal data encrypted at rest and minimised
layer2_standard_saas_catalogue.condition: only if the system stores PII or otherwise sensitive data

layer2_standard_saas_catalogue.nfr: Safety — user-provided files / untrusted input validated (and scanned where relevant) before persistence or processing
layer2_standard_saas_catalogue.condition: only if the system ingests user-provided files or untrusted input

coverage_table.purpose: Before firing the review prompt on an Epic cluster, emit a one-shot coverage table so the reviewer sees what got seeded per category and where it came from.
template: │ TC   │ 8 (+ 2 TODO)  │ test.cases[] across 3 spec files             │
│ NFR  │ 4 (proposed)  │ stack signals: auth + i18n + datastore + e2e │
coverage_table.red_flag: A cluster with **zero DS or zero TC** is a red flag — either the area is genuinely pure glue (no data model, no tests yet) or the scanners missed something (likely on a stack the deterministic scanner doesn't parse). Surface the anomaly in the review prompt — and read the source yourself before concluding — rather than silently proposing an Epic with empty sections.

review_loop.rule: Never write to the SRS backend without confirmation. Drive the loop one cluster at a time.
prompt_template: 🔍 J'ai trouvé <N> éléments pour le domaine `<area>` (scanner + lecture du code). Je te propose de créer :
└─ gaps : <opération sans test>, <vue sans opération liée>
Je pars sur cette structure, ou tu veux retailler l'Epic ? [accept / edit / reject / skip-area]

branches.accept: serialise the cluster as DraftCandidate[] and call `srs-cli.sh write --spec <tmp.json>`
branches.edit: negotiate the title / narrative / FR split and re-confirm
branches.skip-area: park the area and continue with the next

review_loop.throttle: Never batch-accept more than one Epic per prompt — the reviewer has to be able to course-correct cluster by cluster.
